body: This control modifies its own theme, while in most other cases, child controls are modified instead.

I don't think I've encountered warnings for doing this, I used that quite a few times in my module. Perhaps it's because Godot tends to use `int` by default more often even when negative values are not necessary?.

I used `CRASH_COND` here because this function is not supposed to even be called in any other way than in the constructor (it was for code re-use), and it's extremely obvious at development time if that would fail. There is no user code path that would cause it. I could as well remove it by now since I tested the code quite a few times, I only left it to make sure the function remain used that way, and because I prefer to always have a failsafe when accessing raw arrays (since even the debugger doesn't catch it if not going far enough out of bounds).
I can replace it to be totally safe, or wrap it in `DEV_ENABLED`.
I think I implicitely wanted it to come up, so... here it is. Either we could add that right now, or could be done in another PR.
I didn't actually implement it here because the original code treated AtlasTexture differently too. But it depends what we would prefer, maybe it could use the format of the atlas.

I'd say `ERR_FAIL_COND` should still be fine for this, especially if you don't foresee a risk that the contract would easily be broken. Alternatively `DEV_ASSERT`, but it still feels a bit heavy handed to me.
We don't have functions that would fit this exact purpose, so IMO this is fine to implement

Since all images are (currently) expected to either have a complete mip chain or no mipmaps at all, this could be changed to `Image::get_image_required_mipmaps(...)` with the parameters from the `Texture2D` resource. In the future, we could implement the `get_mipmap_count` methods in each `Texture` class

Actually, nevermind. It's not even possible to check if a Texture2D has mipmaps, since unlike the layered and 3d variants it doesn't have a `has_mipmaps` virtual method. This should probably be added (not in this PR though)
